item.title: In a recent interview, Andy Weir, the author of The Martian and Project Hail Mary, shared his thoughts about the progress of AI, how it might affect careers like his in the future and why it could be compared to a homicide hammer.
item.description:
In a recent interview, Andy Weir, the author of The Martian and Project Hail Mary, shared his thoughts about the progress of AI, how it might affect careers like his in the future and why it could be compared to a homicide hammer.
"I think it's only a matter of time," he told SlashFilm. "Honestly, I think I'm lucky that I ended up being a writer right when I did, because I might be among the last generation of fully human writers." Despite that, overall Weir seems to have a positive attitude towards the technology, seeing it as a tool. He points out that other advancements have already surpassed human abilities, like race cars for speed and forklifts for strength, and the smarts of AI falling into a similar category.
"It's a tool that we can use and we can unplug when we don't want to use it," he added. "In the end, if I give you a hammer, you can build a house or you can murder someone. It's not the tool that's the issue; it's the user."
Project Hail Mary Rocky First Look
Not surprisingly, AI is something Weir will explore in his next novel. In a 2024 interview with The Bridge, he teased the project. "I’m working on my next book now. AI plays a significant role in it. But I’m doing it my way, not writing a story about robots falling in love or anything. Writing a story that involves AI is kind of in my wheelhouse because I know how computers work. And I know more about machine learning than most fiction writers, I think. So yes, I’m having some fun with that," he said.
Like fiction and filmmaking, the games industry is also tackling what AI means for the future. Just this week Anthropic blocked AI game clones in a Claude Opus update, Super Smash Bros. creator Masahiro Sakurai declared that AI-made games could never compare to those made by humans, and Epic revealed it had vibe coded a new Epic Games Launcher.
Rachel Weber is the Head of Editorial Development at IGN and an elder millennial. She's been a professional nerd since 2006 when she got her start on Official PlayStation Magazine in the UK, and has since worked for GamesIndustry.Biz, Rolling Stone and GamesRadar. She loves horror, horror movies, horror games, Red Dead Redemption 2, and her Love and Deepspace boyfriends.

item.title: In a November 2 investor relations report, Capcom celebrated the Street Fighter film’s success at the box office during its opening weekend and doubled down on its plan to keep expanding its IP through merchandise, events, esports, and possibly more movies.
item.description:
In a November 2 investor relations report, Capcom celebrated the Street Fighter film’s success at the box office during its opening weekend and doubled down on its plan to keep expanding its IP through merchandise, events, esports, and possibly more movies.
Capcom and Legendary’s Street Fighter movie might’ve hurricane-kicked its way to number one at the box office during its opening weekend, but the stark drop-off it suffered in the following weeks has painted a grim picture for the possibility of a sequel. (The film suffered a 72% drop in its second week, with estimates saying it earned around $91.9 million globally on a reported $80 million budget.)
Despite this, Capcom has celebrated the film’s opening-weekend success with its investors, and says that it remains committed to pursuing its Single Content Multiple Usage strategy.
Street Fighter Images
What exactly is that strategy, you ask? Good question: Capcom announced it in a 2023 integrated report, where it defined the plan as a way to “utilize our popular proprietary content for multiple game platforms” by “actively turning it into movies, theater productions, and other non-game media.” Basically, it means that it's pushing the visibility of its games by ramping up marketing, merchandise, crossovers, and, of course, movies.
In its latest investor relations report, Capcom reaffirmed its intention to continue pursuing this strategy in direct relation to the Street Fighter movie’s opening-week financials.
“In conjunction with the film’s release, Capcom worked to appeal to a broad audience with initiatives that included a worldwide promotional tour, film premiere events in Japan and the U.S., as well as collaborations with game titles, resulting in the film garnering popularity across the globe,” the report reads.
“Capcom is firmly committed to advancing the multifaceted use of its extensive portfolio of game content, guided by its Single Content Multiple Usage strategy, in order to achieve sustainable growth and enhance corporate value.”
This news comes as a mild surprise, given the apparent financial loss on Legendary’s side of things now that two weeks have passed. However, there’s a big push from the talent involved to make another movie, as told to us in several cast interviews. In fact, Olivier Richters — the actor who portrayed Zangief — revealed that the entire cast signed on for three films, which explains why the movie left on such a big cliffhanger and why we saw so little of some of our favorite fighters.
“When they asked me to play Zangief, it was all very clear. There was one goal: Show a [glimpse] of Zangief and his power, so we all want more," he wrote in a YouTube comment. "All actors, including me, signed for three movies. ‘If a sequel is made, Zangief will shine,’ was the promise. Apart from that, you can't expect, from a two-hour movie with so many characters, for everyone to shine in the first part.”
The overall sentiment from fans and movie-goers was rather positive toward the comedic, fist-flinging flick, though critics were less receptive to it overall. IGN scored Street Fighter a 6 out of 10, with reviewer Tom Jorgensen saying it “benefits from a very enthusiastic cast and an anarchic spirit, but Kitao Sakurai’s adaptation of the Capcom games struggles to focus all that energy into a well-told story.”
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: Alien Isolation 2 will be released in 2027, ready to remind you why xenomorphs are pure nightmare fuel. At the Lucca Comics and Games Festival IGN sat down with the game's creative director, Al Hope, who explained the core vision behind the science fiction sequel and why the team was sticking with the survival horror genre.
item.description:
Alien: Isolation 2 will be released in 2027, ready to remind you why xenomorphs are pure nightmare fuel. At the Lucca Comics and Games Festival IGN sat down with the game's creative director, Al Hope, who explained the core vision behind the science fiction sequel and why the team was sticking with the survival horror genre.
"We feel like there's still so much to mine or tap into in the universe of that first movie," he said. "We feel like in Alien: Isolation 2, I think the promise is about transporting you back to that time and place, that window of the timeline where just one alien can be absolutely terrifying and an incredible challenge, an incredible experience."
The original Alien: Isolation, released in 2014, had engineer Amanda (daughter of Ellen) Ripley as its star, as she searched for clues relating to her mother's disappearance on the space station Sevastopol. We've already heard Andrea Deck, Ripley’s voice actor, during a press demo for the sequel, but Hope was keen to underline the fact that Alien Isolation 2 is very focused on its new protagonist.
"We're really proud of Amanda, but to be clear, you're playing as a new character in Isolation 2... She works for the company; she hasn't encountered the creature before. And so yeah, I guess we're super excited about Blake."
We know a little about Blake already. She's a manager at Weyland-Yutani and has just arrived on planet LV-921 in search of the lab that was jettisoned from Sevastopol Station by Amanda Ripley, complete with a xenomorph hanging around inside.
Alien: Isolation 2 Prologue Screenshots
You can read the full interview with Creative Director Al Hope and Project Art Director Ana Sopikova here, where we also talk xenomorph design, seeing the first game's save stations appear in Alien: Romulus, and whether or not the games are now part of the official Alien canon.

item.title: The Long Walk actor Ben Wang is reportedly in talks to play Iceman in the MCU's upcoming X-Men reboot.
item.description:
The Long Walk actor Ben Wang is reportedly in talks to play Iceman in the MCU's upcoming X-Men reboot.
Deadline reported that Wang, who will soon appear as Wyatt Callow in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, is circling the role of Marvel's icy mutant hero, Bobby Drake. He's said to be one of a few other names who have tested for the part, with other allegedly interested names including Gabriel LaBelle (The Fabelmans), Jackson Kelly (The Pitt), and Rhenzy Feliz (The Penguin).
More than anything, news of Wang's potential involvement suggests Marvel at least has plans for Iceman to play a role in the 2028 X-Men film. The character may not have the star power of a Wolverine or Cyclops, but he's remained an important figure in the comic book history for decades. In addition to a variety of appearances throughout animated projects and video games, he was famously played by Shawn Ashmore in live-action movies like the original 2000 X-Men, its two sequels, and X-Men: Days of Future Past.
Wang has found his way to more than a few notable roles in his relatively short amount of time in Hollywood. After playing smaller parts in projects like the MacGyver reboot series, The Last O.G., and 2023's Sight, the actor went on to show up in 2024's Mean Girls and Karate Kid: Legends.
Audiences really started to catch on when he played Hank Olson in the gruesome 2025 adaptation of Stephen King's The Long Walk, with even more set to see what he can do in The Hunger Games prequel later this month. X-Men will surely only open that door further should talks proceed accordingly.
Marvel has already confirmed a small collection of heavy hitters for its upcoming take on classic superhero characters. The list so far includes Inde Navarrette as Rogue, Sadie Sink as Jean Grey, Adam Driver as Mister Sinister, Christopher Abbott as Professor X, Kit Connor as Cyclops, Maya Boyd as Storm, and Samara Weaving as Emma Frost. Gen V actor Asa Germann was reported to have joined as Angel in September.
MCU X-Men Cast as of D23 2026
X-Men is being directed by Thunderbolts* director Jake Schreier and is scheduled to come to theaters May 5, 2028. For now, we'll have to wait to see if Wang lands the part. In the meantime, the old-school X-Men are set to kick off one last hurrah with the release of next month's Avengers: Doomsday. Whether or not Ashmore's Iceman will return for that team-up film remains to be seen.
For more on X-Men, you can see Navarrette tease her take on Rogue's Southern accent. You can also read about what Abbott had to say regarding any cameos between now and 2028.
Photo by Emma McIntyre/Getty Images for IMDb.
Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

item.title: Call of Duty: Warzone is adding a weather system that will make every match feel a bit different.
item.description:
Call of Duty: Warzone is adding a weather system that will make every match feel a bit different.
Later this week, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's Season 1 update will be released, and with it will come big changes to Warzone. Developer Raven Software is adding a bunch of content that matches the mechanics and tone Modern Warfare 4 brought to the franchise last month. One of the biggest things that's coming to Warzone is a new weather system, which means the map might have rain, wind, or other effects when you drop in.
It sounds like the weather will be determined before you ever load into the match, so don't expect weather cycles as you'd see in a game like Grand Theft Auto. The goal is to make it so Warzone matches feel different every time you play, as the battle royale's maps have been pretty stagnant for the last six years. The weather never changes, which can eventually make the maps feel a bit boring. However, this may make the game feel consistently interesting, and something like rain may have slight changes to gameplay. It could impact visibility, make your footsteps louder as they splash in puddles, and more.
Earlier this fall, Wardogs also added weather to multiplayer matches, which had some big changes for the gameplay. It's a worthy change to Call of Duty's battle royale and one that fans have wanted to see for some time. Fans have also wanted to see a day/night cycle as well, which could make something like night-vision goggles a meaningful piece of gear. NVGs are part of the game's DMZ extraction mode, though they're primarily used for enclosed facilities that have no power.
The new Call of Duty: Warzone update will launch with two new maps on November 6 as part of Modern Warfare 4 Season 1.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Epic's rivalry with Valve isn't anything new, but while it's usually CEO Tim Sweeney taking shots at Valve, an ex-engineer posted a long list of problems Steam has caused in the industry.
item.description:
Epic's rivalry with Valve isn't anything new, but while it's usually CEO Tim Sweeney taking shots at Valve, an ex-engineer posted a long list of problems Steam has caused in the industry.
Just last week, after posting about Valve's 30% cut that it takes off the top of game sales, ex-Epic Engineer Kiaran Ritchie wrote a long Twitter post detailing his critiques of the biggest PC games marketplace. And, really, it seems like he's throwing up his hands and accepting Valve's dominion over the ecosystem while blaming Steam users.
Ritchie says that, "even if an alternative were objectively better, by whatever metric you care about, it would still be of no interest to Steam users. They would in fact find it to be a problem and a threat to their investment." Specifically, he claims Steam users are hostile to other stores even existing, by saying, "Competition in this space is not only uninteresting to most Steam users, it's actively denigrated! The CONSEQUENCE of this situation, is that 30% of all gross revenue is siphoned out of the PC games industry into a black hole."
Steam Machine – Hands On Photos
Epic Games has tried its hands at unseating Steam again recently, after Tim Sweeney bragged on Twitter about vibe coding a new version of the Epic Games Store that launches faster than Steam. But, while launching quickly and letting people access their library without waiting minutes is an improvement, even Ritchie doesn't feel like it'll make much of a difference.
Elsewhere in the post, Ritchie says, "The Steam client and infrastructure is somewhere between 'not that hard' and 'trivial.' It's a download service attached to a payment processor with a smattering of services on the side. Cloud providers handle all the infrastructure these days." But even if someone makes a 'better' client, he says, "Steam users love Steam and having their whole library in one place. It works. It's dependable. It has sales, and cards, and achievements, oh my!"
This all comes on top of Epic's years-long battle to lower the amount of cash marketplaces take from digital sales. Epic hasn't only fought Valve on this; the company has also taken on Apple and Google in its quest to get Fortnite on mobile devices – and then had to pay Apple $6 million, but won against Google.
But with Valve, Epic's problem seems to be that most gamers prefer Steam outright. After all, there are dozens of game stores on PC where people can buy games, but as Ritchie points out, Steam users are happy just sticking with Valve's store. And no matter what Epic does, that probably isn't going to change.

item.title: On November 2, former Xbox COO Helen Chiang took to LinkedIn to “set the record straight” about rumors over her exit from Microsoft.
item.description:
On November 2, former Xbox COO Helen Chiang took to LinkedIn to “set the record straight” about rumors over her exit from Microsoft.
Chiang, who was promoted as Xbox’s first-ever chief operating officer in July, had been with the company for 21 years, previously serving as the head of Minecraft. Her exit from the role in late October — just three months after the position was created — came as a shock to both industry veterans and fans alike.
Eurogamer reported that Chiang had allegedly been "terminated for policy violations." A week later, Chiang spoke out to share her side of the story in a lengthy post on LinkedIn titled "Clarity is Kindness."
The 100 Best Xbox Games of All Time
In her post, Chiang said rumors of this supposed policy violation were “not accurate,” and claimed that the discourse surrounding her departure from Xbox has “created a picture of me that I hardly recognize.”
She strongly denied accusations of “leaking confidential company information to the press,” saying she’s never spoken to journalists outside of interviews approved by Xbox. She also denied rumors that she left the company to join a competitor, and pushed back on allegations of “engaging in discrimination, bullying, harassment, insider trading, embezzlement, or other fraudulent activity,” or leaving because she was “passed over for a bigger role.”
“I stand by my record: both the results I delivered and the way I have treated people throughout my career. I won’t let speculation define my character or erase that record,” she wrote.
“I believe in fairness, accountability, and holding ourselves to the standards we expect of others. Those standards only mean something when they’re applied consistently. I have serious concerns about how they were applied in my case, and I believe those concerns deserve to be taken seriously.
“I share this because I don’t want my departure reduced to an inaccurate story about incompetence, ambition for the next big job, or a Nelson-level scandal. My story is about staying true to your core values, especially when it is hard. That’s the legacy I hope to leave behind.”
She ended her post by saying that this was “not how I ever imagined my story here would end,” saying, “it is not the whole story.”
IGN has asked Microsoft for comment.

item.title: Borderlands developer Gearbox has called on fans to let it know what they want next from the next game in the franchise, as work begins on “an exciting overall direction.”
item.description:
Borderlands developer Gearbox has called on fans to let it know what they want next from the next game in the franchise, as work begins on “an exciting overall direction.”
Borderlands 4 just wrapped up its Year 1 of DLC, and in a note to fans today, Gearbox issued its long-awaited future content announcement, confirming more is coming to the looter shooter next year. “Moving forward, Weekly Activity refreshes and Community Challenges will continue,” Gearbox said. “We just wrapped our Year 1 roadmap, and the team is cooking hard on more Borderlands 4 content for next year.” What this content involves beyond Weekly Activity refreshes and Community Challenges was not specified.
Gearbox then spoke vaguely about its plans for the future of the Borderlands franchise, asking fans for their opinions.
“The team is constantly listening to community feedback, and they are exploring additional character arcs, storylines, and an exciting overall direction for the future of the franchise,” Gearbox said.
The studio continued: “... we’re also taking a bigger look at the franchise as a whole. Where can we take it next? What characters do you want to spend more time with? What stories deserve a payoff? A huge part of that is listening to you. Keep the conversation going - we're listening. Tell us what you think! Share your thoughts with us on social and tune into the Gearbox Devcast. We’re always responding to community feedback on that show.”
Don’t hold your breath for the announcement of Borderlands 5 or whatever the next game ends up being called, however. It sounds like early days.
“All that said, big plans take time, and we need some room to work,” Gearbox added. “You can trust that we’ll talk more when the time is right. Now is your chance to influence what we’ll say. We’re listening and we’re working hard for you. Thanks for being with us in the Borderlands.”
The announcement comes as the Borderlands franchise crossed 100 million units sold. Over the summer, fans were questioning how well Borderlands 4 had done not just in terms of launch sales, but continuing player base, and how that might have affected Gearbox's plans, as they waited for confirmation of a second year of support.
Since launching in September, Borderlands 4 has suffered various controversies, mostly to do with severe PC performance issues. Outspoken CEO Randy Pitchford went on the offensive, responding directly to complaints on social media to Claptrap back at disgruntled fans.
Strauss Zelnick, boss of Gearbox parent company Take-Two, previously admitted that Borderlands 4 sales had suffered “a little bit of softness” as a result of the technical issues, but expressed confidence “it’ll all be made up” given enough time. The Nintendo Switch 2 version was scrapped, with Take-Two saying Gearbox had prioritized continued "improvements" to the game on its existing platforms.
All the while, Borderlands 4 remains on a ‘mixed’ user review rating on Steam. After launching to over 300,000 concurrent players on Valve’s platform, Borderlands 4 now averages a concurrent peak in the four digits. Steam numbers do not paint the entire picture of a game’s popularity as it’s also on consoles, but it’s clear Borderlands 4 could do with a shot in the arm.

item.title: Nintendo has explained why it chose to develop another The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.
item.description:
Nintendo has explained why it chose to develop another The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.
Franchise producer Eiji Aonuma was asked what sparked the team's desire to return to one of the most treasured stories in gaming history during the first installment in a series of Ask the Developer Q&A posts. It's an in-depth chat about what it was like to revisit a classic game for Nintendo Switch 2, and how it came about in the first place.
The reimagining set to launch in just a few short days will mark the second time Nintendo has remade The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (the first launched for the Nintendo 3DS in 2011). Aonuma explained that there were a number of factors Entertainment Planning & Development (EDP) Production Group No. 3 had in mind, with its 40th anniversary being one of the most important.
60 The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Switch 2 Screenshots
"This year marks the 40th anniversary of the very first Legend of Zelda game," Aonuma said. "With that in mind, I was thinking about what I should create as the producer of the series. Many of the team members who work alongside me on Legend of Zelda games today have only experienced developing the more recent titles. That led me to wonder, 'Do they truly understand just how significant The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time was to the series as a whole?'"
Aonuma makes a good point. Although he worked on the original Nintendo 64 game when it launched in 1998 and has carried that experience through subsequent entries in the series in the decades since, there are plenty of team members who don't have that same familiarity with its past.
Sure, there are those with a passing familiarity with the original The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time or those who have at least played it, but Aonuma started to wonder how they'd interpret the game "as they go about developing future Legend of Zelda games." Allowing them to not only revisit that original story but also leave their own stamp on it, he believes, could help bolster whatever new The Legend of Zelda games come next.
"By learning the game structure and development style behind the original The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, and by actually rebuilding it as a full remake," he added, "it may trigger new insights that they can carry forward into future development. If we could achieve that, I thought it would be incredibly valuable. That’s what led us to the conclusion that now is the right time to revisit The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time once again."
Aonuma elaborated, saying that there were many elements considered when choosing to develop a The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2. The team wanted players who had grown used to the open structure of games like Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom to enjoy the fun of "progressing through a carefully paced adventure and story" that is "gradually building up the player’s growth and their understanding of the narrative along the way."
Which classic Zelda game do you most want a remake of?

item.title: The entirety of 2026 has been marked by continually rising hardware prices, and now, according to the latest Steam Hardware Survey, the average gaming PC is starting to embrace older hardware once more.
item.description:
The entirety of 2026 has been marked by continually rising hardware prices, and now, according to the latest Steam Hardware Survey, the average gaming PC is starting to embrace older hardware once more.
The October Steam Hardware Survey went live yesterday, and it's clear that the state of PC hardware is causing gamers to be a bit more frugal with their builds. The biggest sign of this is in the RAM configuration, where systems using 16GB of RAM have now taken the top spot, rising 3.6% to cover 41.42% of the Steam user base. Users with a 32GB configuration have diminished at the same time, dropping 5.16%, to cover 37.06% of Steam users.
But it's not just RAM that people are cutting back on. For graphics cards, the RTX 3060 has reclaimed its top spot, growing 0.08%, and now representing 3.62% of all Steam users. That doesn't seem like a lot, but considering the huge amount of GPUs that exist, it's a significant proportion. It probably doesn't hurt that you can get an RTX 3060 used on eBay for around $250–300 right now. For CPUs, 8-core CPUs saw a decline in favor of 4-core CPUs, which rose 1.57% to cover 12.36% of PCs with Steam.
EVGA RTX 3060 XC Black Review
It's not hard to see why people are opting for less powerful PCs right now. Pretty much every PC component has gone up in price over the last year, to the point where high-end GPUs are flat-out disappearing from retailer's listings.
Meanwhile, Samsung's latest earnings report suggests that the RAM crisis is only going to get worse next year, as that company gears up to forward even more memory to AI data centers. And while all of this is going on, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman even came out and suggested that it's 'quite terrible' for people to have RAM in their own computers.
It's not just gaming PCs that are getting hit by this ongoing RAM crisis. The PS5 Pro sold out ahead of GTA 6, prompting retailers to charge upwards of $1,399 for used consoles, and Microsoft started asking people to sell unused Xboxes. In the face of all this, it becomes less shocking when rumors appear suggesting that the next-generation Xbox is going to cost $1,800.
But at least when faced with these higher RAM prices, PC builders have the choice to opt for a lower-end configuration, and that's exactly what's happening with the latest Steam Hardware Survey.

item.title: Fifteen years after its initial release, one of the internet's most infamous cult horror movies, Megan Is Missing, has unexpectedly gained a sequel, and fittingly, it's available for free on Instagram.
item.description:
Fifteen years after its initial release, one of the internet's most infamous cult horror movies, Megan Is Missing, has unexpectedly gained a sequel, and fittingly, it's available for free on Instagram.
Megan Is Missing: Evil Never Dies was written and directed by original filmmaker Michael Goi. After being quietly released in episodes and teasers by Goi, cast members, and influencers, the complete project is now fully accessible online.
"For years, people have asked me to continue the story of Megan Is Missing. But it never seemed to be the right time. Until now," Goi told Dread Central.
“Megan Is Missing: Evil Never Dies gives me the opportunity to use the vertical format in ways that increase the audience’s proximity to the terror they are seeing. It brings them closer to disturbing events and makes them part of what is happening to the characters.”
Spoilers for Megan is Missing and plot details for Megan Is Missing: Evil Never Dies below.
Released originally in 2011, Megan Is Missing centered on high schoolers Megan and Amy, whose lives spiral into a cautionary-tale-style nightmare after Megan connects with an online stranger. Framed through found footage, video chats, and webcam feeds, it gained widespread notoriety for its dark subject matter and bleak climax. It initially flew under the radar but attracted public attention in 2020 on TikTok, leading Goi to share a public warning regarding the movie's brutal scenes.
In the sequel, original stars Rachel Quinn and Amber Perkins play a version of their real-world selves, invited to appear on a podcast. Unfortunately, the host is not who he seems and has sinister intentions for the pair. You can head to Instagram to binge all 36 episodes right now.

item.title: Nintendo has revealed the development team responsible for creating The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.
item.description:
Nintendo has revealed the development team responsible for creating The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.
The Super Mario Bros. company typically keeps its cards pretty close to its chest when it comes to the behind-the-scenes details for its biggest releases. The Legend of Zelda series is no exception, but Nintendo did offer a peek behind the curtain as part of an Ocarina of Time remake installment in its Ask the Developer Q&A series.
Fans have speculated who might be behind the Nintendo Switch 2 reimagining of an all-time classic since it was announced. While some believed Xenoblade series developer Monolith Soft might be leading the charge, for example, the interview confirmed that it's actually Nintendo's Entertainment Planning & Development (EDP) Production Group No. 3 that's responsible for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.
Featured in the first interview chapter are franchise producer Eiji Aonuma and series directing veteran Hidemaro Fujibayashi, with EDP Production Group No. 3's HokWai Ng, Aya Shida, Hiroki Taguchi, and Masato Ohashi also listed as interviewees to be featured in future highlights. In other words, the core team behind one of the most highly-anticipated games of the last few years is the same group behind most The Legend of Zelda projects from the last 30 years.
Longtime fans of the original Nintendo 64 game (or even its 2011 Nintendo 3DS remake) who have feared the Switch 2 version of the story could tarnish its reputation can probably rest easy knowing it was in experienced hands. That said, it is always possible another team like Monolith Soft could have chipped in as a support developer, though we likely won't know the full list of team members until we have a better look at those credits in a few days.
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launches for Switch 2 November 5. Although it was made by the same hands that have helped keep the classic fantasy franchise kicking for decades, that doesn't mean the developers weren't willing to experiment where they could. During the interview, Aonuma explained that he tried to "basically let the developers make whatever changes they genuinely felt were necessary."
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Preview Screenshots
"I wanted the team to make The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time their own, and to follow through on their own ideas about what the game should be," he added. "That said, I did deliver my fair share of lectures along the way. (Laughs) I took a step back to observe how the younger members of the development team would reimagine The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time using the insights and answers they had arrived at on their own."
Fujibayashi added that, from his point of view, it was important for the team to have a clear outline for what would and wouldn't be changed from the Nintendo 64 game early on.
"For people like us, who know both the original The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and the recent 3D Legend of Zelda games, there's no shortage of things we’d like to say when it comes to designing a game," he said. "(Laughs) That’s why I took a step back and supported the team from a broader perspective by helping them clarify the things they needed to be mindful of when designing the game."
Nintendo Switch 2: The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Edition Console Images
Despite having a good plan for how Nintendo and EDP Production Group No. 3 would tackle The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake from the get-go, Aonuma recently admitted that he's still a bit nervous to see how fans will respond. Meanwhile, Google recently launched a time-traveling Easter Egg to help build up hype for this week's new Switch 2 game.
Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

item.title: World of Warcraft Forever is just a few days away, and Blizzard has confirmed the global release times and preload details. Here's when you can play in your timezone.
item.description:
World of Warcraft Forever is just a few days away, and Blizzard has confirmed the global release times and preload details.
WoW Forever launches on November 4, and has a global release scheduled, which means everyone will be able to start playing at the same time, no matter where they are. This is super important in an MMO like WoW, because it means that one region isn't able to get significantly further ahead than any other.
World of Warcraft Forever Global Release Times
Because World of Warcraft Forever has a global release, all you really have to do is look at its official release time of 3pm PST and convert that to your own timezone. However, because of the nature of a global release, depending on where you are in the world, the game will either be launching on November 4 or on November 5.
Los Angeles: 3pm PST
Mexico City: 5pm CST
New York: 6pm EST
London: 11pm GMT
Beijing: 7am CST (November 5)
Seoul: 8am KST (November 5)
Tokyo: 8am JST (November 5)
Melbourne: 10:00am AEST (November 5)
World of Warcraft: Forever Screenshots
World of Warcraft Forever Preload Details
World of Warcraft Forever is available to preload now. Simply open or download the Battle.net launcher, then WoW Forever should show up in the 'Favorites' bar by default. If it doesn't, go to 'Games' and then search for 'World of Warcraft.' Then, click the WoW icon, go to 'game version' and ensure 'WoW Forever' is selected, and then hit the big blue 'Install' button.
Once it's downloaded you'll be good to log in when the servers go live on November 4 at 3pm PST.
How Much Space Will You Need For World of Warcraft Forever?
According to Blizzard's system requirements, World of Warcraft Forever will need at least 128GB of available space, but I'd actually reserve a bit extra. Just like any version of WoW, there are going to be hundreds of mods available from day one, and unless you're looking to play the game entirely with the default UI, you're going to want to make sure you have some space for add-ons. I'd recommend having at least 150GB reserved for Forever, just in case. Note, as well, that Blizzard specifically calls out an SSD, rather than a harddrive.
World of Warcraft Forever minimum PC requirements:
CPU: '4 cores, 3GHz processor (Intel Haswell or Ryzen Zen)' – think Intel Core i5 4460 / AMD Ryzen 5 1600X
GPU: 'DirectX 12 Capable 4GB GPU, GTX 10-series or RDNA 1' – Think Nvidia GeForce GTX 1060 / AMD Radeon RX 5600
Storage: 128GB SSD
World of Warcraft Forever recommended PC requirements:
CPU: '8 performance cores, 5.2GHz boost clock; Intel Core Ultra (series 2) or AMD Ryzen Zen 5' – think Intel Core Ultra 5 265K / AMD Ryzen 5 9600X
GPU: 'DirectX 12 capable 8GB GPU; Nvidia RTX 40 series/AMD RDNA 3/Intel Arc B-Series' – think Nvidia GeForce RTX 4060 / AMD Radeon RX 7600 / Intel Arc B570
Storage: 128GB SSD
While you wait to play, be sure to check out our big interview with Blizzard on its plans for World of Warcraft: Forever post-launch, which include update frequency and new locations.

item.title: British self-made millionaire, entrepreneur, and social media educator Mark Tilbury put out a video giving the most sound financial advice of 2026: buy GTA 6. According to him, it’ll save you a big chunk of change.
item.description:
British self-made millionaire, entrepreneur, and social media educator Mark Tilbury put out a video giving the most sound financial advice of 2026: buy GTA 6. According to him, it’ll save you a big chunk of change.
“GTA 6 costs $99.99,” he said, going straight for the more expensive Ultimate Edition rather than the $80 standard edition (perhaps he, like many others, consider the Ultimate Edition and its extra contents to be the default version). “If it takes you 80 hours to complete, that’s $1.25 per hour of fun. But once you add in side missions and explore the map, it’s down to 50 cents an hour.
“Now let’s say you play for four hours every evening, that’s 50 nights of entertainment. Compare that to going out, where you could easily spend $100 in a single night. That’s why buying GTA 6 actually saves you $5,000.”
Obviously the video is tongue-in-cheek and not actual financial advice (who’s going out 50 nights in a row and spending $100 a pop?). But it’s actually a fair point on the value proposition of the game. An investment in your time, if you will.
That’s why publishers are reportedly hoping GTA 6 sets a new precedent on game pricing — other companies will struggle to compete with its size and scale. It seems like the kind of game you could play for hundreds of hours, and that’s before GTA Online even comes into the equation.
“I’m a 40yo gamer, don't drink much, don't smoke, don't do drugs or go out with friends,” said one commenter. “This is how I explain me gaming to people.”
In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023
“Straight to mum,” said another. “Rockstar paid a billion dollars for it, so it’s a steal at the end of the day,” said another mathematician.
Tilbury is a businessman best known for his videos on frugal living. Despite being a millionaire, he reuses old cups, flies economy, wears the same rotation of clothes, and avoids luxury hotels.
We’ve got plenty more on GTA 6 while you wait for its November 19 release date, including an unlikely gameplay reveal in the latest episode of South Park, how GTA 6 named one of its biggest mechanics after a beloved GTA 4 meme, and how GTA 6's map will open up relatively early and let you explore freely.

item.title: Edgerunners 2 showrunner Bartosz Sztybor on all things Cyberpunk, including V's apparent appearance, canon endings, and more.
item.description:
Edgerunners, the hugely popular Netflix anime set in CD Projekt’s Cyberpunk 2077 world, takes what’s great about the video game and expertly translates it into the world of animation. The recently released Season 2 told its own story — one we know is set just a year after the events of the main game, in 2078 (more on this later) — and it all wraps up nicely. But wait! Was that a tease for V in the show? And, if that’s true, does that mean there’s an ending of Cyberpunk 2077 that CD Projekt considers canon, and thus acts as the jumping off point for all post-game spinoffs like Edgerunners 2?
At the Lucca Comics and Games festival, we got the chance to put all this to Edgerunners writer, producer, and showrunner Bartosz Sztybor, who did his best to answer without giving much of the game away. And speaking of giving the game away, what about that Season 3?
The world of Cyberpunk is set to expand further, of course, with the in-development Cyberpunk 2 (where and when the game takes place is yet to be announced). There's also a live-action film in the works, although according to CD Projekt, the Cyberpunk 2077 movie won't retrace the game's steps.
IGN: Eagle-eyed fans spotted that in the scene in the data archive, there's a wall of images and there's one that looks like it may be female V. Was that intentional, or something left to interpretation?
Bartosz Sztybor: It's left for interpretation. But also the dialogue that they're having there is, I think, very important. So yeah, it's left for interpretation.
Yeah I ain’t crazy that’s deadass V https://t.co/3XC5KtlrDa
IGN: Easter eggs from the game, is that an important thing for you all to include?
Bartosz Sztybor: It's not important at all. That's why I wouldn't call it Easter eggs. I think that's the way we are trying to create a franchise for Cyberpunk. So, to create standalone stories that are self-sufficient, that you can just read one comic book and you are having the catharsis and you don't need to know any other comic book or a game or other stuff. But we are putting those things that are not as a fan service, but for the audience or the readers to feel that this world is alive. That's why we don't want to create anime or animation or a comic book that will need the audience to read three other comic books and two TV shows to understand why this guy is a villain. But I like to put those many things like Sal Bigelow in Edgerunners 2, who was what, five years earlier in the comic book Cyberpunk: Big City Dreams. But only if there’s a reason.
So it's never thinking that, oh, what we should put in this scene to make fans happy? It's about building a bigger narrative.
IGN: When you are setting something after the game, after 2077, do you have conversations with CDPR about a canon ending for the game, that would set up a world state for Edgerunners 2? Or is it more kind of abstract than that?
Bartosz Sztybor: It's both, I would say. It's not like super abstract, but also, we don't want to set a canon ending. So there were a lot of conversations again with the lore team to see what we can do to somehow satisfy all the endings, and what will be the state of the world after the game. That's why the scene that you asked about, we don't want to be straightforward, but we are giving some suggestions that will probably reveal the state of the world in more comic books and other stuff. So there are discussions. There are discussions, but we are not setting one kind of ending.
Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 Images
IGN: When you're writing these stories, do you have a set canon in mind, or is it a little bit more variable than that?
Bartosz Sztybor: There is canon, of course. But again, when we were creating Edgerunners 1 and multiple comic books and board games, the canon was before the game. So we knew the state of the world. And for the things post-game, it's not that there are super detailed canon things, but one important canon information is that Arasaka is weakened and that's it. And it gives us a lot of opportunities to show the city in a different way.
But again, it's not detailed. So it doesn't make any of the endings canon. But the things that happened in the game could lead to that, whatever your choice was.
IGN: Is that something in your mind that you're trying to stay away from things that would be too specific in terms of setting up new canon?
Bartosz Sztybor: Yeah. It's the same thing that I answered about the characters. There are some IP that are created in a way — I won't mention the name — that are created in a way... And I think that the goal of CDPR, the way we want to create franchises for The Witcher and Cyberpunk is to, again, create standalone stories. So you have a graphic novel and you can read it from the start to finish. You don't need to know anything about the world, but you can have the Easter eggs or some connections that build the world, that show you that, okay, this world exists. And I prefer to create a franchise like that.
I like fans who find those things. There’s a comic book called You Have My Word, and there was a fixer [Arthur Cormac] that you saw in Edgerunners 1. And I think only 20 or 30 fans found that. And then that fixer also had a cameo in another comic book. And those three things happen at different times.
So as a fan, you can create their story, you can connect the dots. And I think this is the best way to create a franchise, because you let the fans stay with the story, think about the story, and you don't give them answers. You just give them questions and they can connect things.
So I don't know if I answered the question, but I think that's the way we want to create the franchise.
IGN: What are your thoughts right now on a potential Edgerunners 3? Is it something that you are open to and maybe just waiting for a story? What are your feelings on that right now?
Bartosz Sztybor: When writing Season 1, I was already thinking about other seasons, about other stories because there's a lot of stories to tell. Always when I'm creating, I'm searching for answers to questions that I don't know how to answer. So I knew that after Season 1, I didn't answer all the questions. So there was a dream of creating more seasons.
But I think it's always with CDPR, only if there's a perfect story and perfect people to deliver, then we can do it. And after Season 1, Studio Trigger said, "No, we are just too tired." But then here in Lucca, right after the release of Season 1, we talked with Studio Trigger and they said, "Okay, we are not that tired anymore, so maybe we should do it." And I already had ideas. So two months later I presented a pitch to them, because also they said we don't want to do a sequel, like a classic sequel.
And we have CDPR and we as well, we didn't want to do that as well. We wanted to do something different. So when I presented them a pitch for Season 2, they were super impressed and that's why Season 3 happened. I think that's the same story with Season 3. So I have some stories, but we need to see. If there's no studio or director with a vision like Ikarashi, it doesn't make sense. We don't want to do things that will be mediocre or not good enough. So the ideas are there, but I’m also with how Season 2 completes Season 1. So I think as a package, it already works.

item.title: Google just got a The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Easter egg that transports you back to the 1998 version of the search engine — complete with blue links for results.
item.description:
Google just got a The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Easter egg that transports you back to the 1998 version of the search engine — complete with blue links for results.
The remake of the Nintendo 64 classic comes out this Thursday, November 5, but you can find the secret on Google now if you type “zelda” into the search bar and press enter. This makes the Master Sword appear in the bottom-right corner of the screen.
Click the Master Sword and it gets shoved into its pedestal, an audio effect plays, and the screen distorts to pull you through time. Now you’re back at the old, useful, minimalist Google that showed search results as a series of blue links for people to click on.
What you’re seeing is Google from 1998, the year the original Ocarina of Time launched. It was the year of the Saving Private Ryan movie, the rise of teen pop icons like Britney Spears and breakthrough television shows like Sex and the City. The Boy Is Mine by Brandy and Monica would have been blasting from the stereos of passing cars, kids would have been playing with Furbys, and everyone was rocking a Nokia. Ah, nostalgia. Google’s 1998 version even has the “I’m feeling lucky” option, which would just take you to a random search result.
As Nintendo has pulled back the curtain on The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, we’ve begun to get a better understanding of how this Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive will look and feel to play. IGN has already got you covered with an extensive hands-on preview, as well as a roundup of all the changes we’ve noticed so far compared to the N64 masterpiece.
While you wait, check out a special episode of Nintendo Voice Chat where we dive deeper into our Zelda preview. Meanwhile, Eiji Aonuma, producer of the Zelda series at Nintendo, recently admitted some of the younger members of his team had never played the original game, but insisted that was very much a good thing for the development of the remake.
Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

item.title: Elon Musk has joined the growing backlash over OpenAI CEO Sam Altman's recent comments on RAM.
item.description:
Elon Musk has joined the growing backlash over Sam Altman’s recent comments on RAM.
Last week, the OpenAI CEO sparked outrage across the internet and, specifically, within the gamer community, when he said he thought it was “terrible” for people to have RAM in their PCs rather than a data center.
In an interview with YouTuber Cheeky Pint, Altman said: "From a global allocation perspective, actually, it's quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world's limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer, and being used 5% of the time. Like, you want maximum utilization in the cloud if you're trying to deal with this very supply constrained environment. And somehow many people's intuition is the opposite of that."
The comments have been widely ridiculed, with many suggesting that, whether he intended it or not, Altman sounds like he wants to take away personal ownership of memory and force society to use resources for the benefit of AI companies such as his. Social media was flooded with posts, images, and videos of people slamming Altman for the suggestion, promising to protect their precious memory from any who might try to claim it. Others have simply dunked on Altman for the comments, with countless memes and, yes, AI-generated videos showing the AI billionaire in various states of embarrassment.
Here’s 576GB worth of go f*ck yourself Sam Altman https://t.co/X4ewhFK0cp
Using a stick of RAM to stir my coffee this morning, fuck you, Sam Altman
sam altman: your ram should be in data centersme with 32 gigs of ram: https://t.co/0VR1kvgtxO
Found on reddit. Hilarious https://t.co/43Exuo1b3r
Speaking of AI billionaires, his tech rival, Elon Musk, got in on the act with a meme of his own, letting his millions of followers know where he stands on the subject of memory ownership.
"The people deserve to have their RAM too!" Musk declared in a post on X, the social media platform he owns, alongside a meme of Colonel Hans Landa from Quentin Tarantino’s 2009 film Inglourious Basterds.
The people deserve to have their RAM too! https://t.co/q6dwauALw4
The AI boom has led to a scarcity of memory to power it, which in turn has caused graphics cards, video game consoles, and PC components to skyrocket in price. Sony, Microsoft, and Nintendo have all raised the prices of their consoles as a result of the ‘RAMpocalypse,’ while the RTX 5080 just disappeared off of Nvidia's marketplace, weeks after the RTX 5090 was all but discontinued.
Microsoft reportedly expects its next-gen Xbox, codenamed Project Helix, to cost as much as $1,800. Sony has yet to announce its next-gen hardware, but analysts suspect it will push back its launch for as long as possible amid cost concern.
Altman, though, is unlikely to change his line of thinking any time soon. He’s currently on the hunt for up to $20 billion in a new funding round co-led by UAE investors, down from an earlier target of about $30 billion, according to CNBC.
Nvidia GeForce RTX 5080 – Photos
While Musk is happy to take shots at Altman, he’s having AI problems of his own. In a remarkable tweet, the Tesla and SpaceX owner appeared to admit to throttling Grok Bot for being “unsustainably” expensive. Users had complained there were hitting limits sooner than expected, and Musk replied to one such complaint to say the cost of running the AI agent was “unsustainably high relative to revenue.”
This in turn sparked an explosion of comments across social media, with many suggesting Musk's admission here signalled a significant issue with the economics of generative AI itself. Grok Bot, launched in beta in August with paid weekly active users nearing 800,000 by late October. The agent runs autonomous tasks on virtual computers, demanding far more compute than simple chatbots. Heavy users faced sudden lockouts and frustration, with some canceling plans.
In a follow-up tweet replying to one person highlighting the potential impact of Musk's statement, he said: "Just being sensible."
Photo by Heather Diehl/Getty Images. Photo by Kent NISHIMURA / AFP via Getty Images.

item.title: Niftski, the speedrunning world record holder for Super Mario Bros., beat his own record on a Halloween livestream while dressed as Mario. Speaking in character, he said: “Hopefully I don’t get this today because that would be very stupid.” Guess what?
item.description:
Niftski, the speedrunning world record holder for Super Mario Bros., beat his own record on a Halloween livestream while dressed as Mario. Speaking in character, he said: “Hopefully I don’t get this today because that would be very stupid.” Guess what?
This Halloween run, which you can watch on Niftski's YouTube channel, shaved 0.33 seconds off the previous world record, also held by Niftski — two frames away from a perfect run.
4:54.299 SMB1 ANY% WORLD RECORD ON HALLOWEEN WHILE LARPING AS MARIO! It doesn't even feel real that I actually achieved this, but here we are. Only 2 frames (33 milliseconds) stand between this run and absolute perfection / TAS tie. 4:54.265 next! https://t.co/S1ZpmEMG4c
According to Niftski, those two frames were lost early in the run and kept him away from a “perfect run,” theorized to be the absolute pinnacle of Super Mario Bros. “any percent” attempts. He messed up fast accelerations in the first and second rooms by a small amount which cost one frame each.
If it is accurate and there are no more strats to bring the time down significantly, that just leaves the run and those two frames. That means there’s only two milliseconds left, which means there are only two more world records possible in the category.
“Will this be like the first ever game perfected? Like what's gonna happen once someone matches the TAS? It's just over?” asked one fan.
Niftski breaks the SMB1 world record while doing the worst Mario impression ever. Frame-perfect hands, not-so-perfect voice 🍄 https://t.co/B21YnDkrwH
Niftski sits alone at the top of the speedrunning records, and it seems the only person who can beat him is himself, dressed as Mario. He holds the records for warpless, glitchless, and the “any percent” category, which is a race to the end by any means necessary, skipping whatever you can using exploits and glitches.
It’s that last category he beat this Halloween, taking his previous record of 4:54:332 down to 4:54:229 — that’s minutes, seconds, and milliseconds. About halfway through the run, he committed fully to Mario and let Nintendo fill his heart.
According to the speedrunner, being a doofus and pretending to be Mario helped. “It made me not nervous at all,” said Niftski, “it doesn’t even feel real. It felt so casual.”
“I can't believe I witnessed a russian mario do the 67 and get any% wr in the same video,” said one X / Twitter user who watched the stream.
Image credit: Niftski / YouTube.
